title: The 10X Programmer, and other Myths
summary: Interview with Laurent Bossavit: the 10x programmer, exponential defect-cost curve and 'software crisis' rest on thin, circular or invented evidence.

assertions.quote: in many cases the research was done on very small groups and was not extremely representative
I could not find any solid proof that someone had measured something and came up with those fantastic costs

verdicts.note: Boehm's original data exists but is thinner than the derived charts; modern iterative projects show much flatter curves.

assertions.quote: I think the crisis is very much over-exploited, very overblown

verdicts.note: Standish CHAOS figures are widely criticised; failure definitions vary so much that no robust rate exists.

Despite software being 'notoriously known for cost overruns', the review found no general tendency to overoptimism and only ~20% median overrun for larger projects, supporting the view that crisis figures overstate the problem; the opinion-survey mechanism is not discussed.

assertions.quote: it takes a lot more energy to debunk a claim than it takes to just make things up

verdicts.note: A sociological explanation, not a measurable prediction.

Uncovering the flaws in one well-regarded study took the reproduction team about 5 person-months (over 6 months elapsed), while the original result had already spread through 119 citations, most repeating it as a causal effect; supports the asymmetry between asserting and debunking, says nothing about fashion.

assertions.quote: they act as curiosity stoppers, basically

verdicts.note: A framing claim about how folklore affects inquiry.
